boundaries: Apply the player’s selected content boundaries; offer a less intense presentation where needed.
completion_conditions: Edda is recovered to a safe ledge and the rescuers have withdrawn from the threatened crossing, or the attempt has ended with the rescuers on safe ground and Edda's observed loss or last known position recorded. Simply assigning a rescue or announcing an intention to leave is insufficient.
The survey notebook is in a named holder's custody, left at its known position or lost through play; recovery of a dropped notebook is optional after rescue.

A failed rescue closes with the loss report, without a compulsory assault on the raider camp.

outcomes.outcome: This adventure has reached its authored closing event with the actual successes or losses acknowledged. Its earned result and continuing consequences remain true.

failure_conditions: Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.
Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

gm_guidance.instructions:
Use this Plan as private preparation within Severed Lands. Ground play in the accepted party and starting facts. The named new people and incidents belong to this adventure; existing Setting facts and earned consequences remain authoritative. Give the player concrete information for a first decision, follow their chosen approach, and keep private answers concealed until discovered.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.
gm_guidance.player_freedom: Objectives express opportunities, not mandatory conduct. A refusal, changed allegiance or early discovery can change the route or end the job. Carry forward established consequences instead of restoring a preferred plot.
gm_guidance.preparation_detail: Read this preparation and its relevant Setting sources. Keep a concise record of named promises, discovered evidence, lost resources and NPC attitudes. The preparation contains the core answer and resolutions; incidental dialogue and connective description remain the GM’s work.
gm_guidance.railroading: Conclude after the bounded problem and immediate aftermath are resolved. Offer a short epilogue choice; begin a further adventure only if the player asks to continue.

facts.fact: The party is on a broad Cairnfields ledge. Surveyor Edda Sorn hangs ten feet below a rope crossing, caught in a harness tied to the near-side winch.
A raider lookout occupies the approach above the winch. A second raider is visible on the far side; neither has attacked the party. A lower shelf could arrest a short fall.

advancement.allocation: The Player Character and Companions start and remain at level 2. Story success, defeat, combat and optional jobs never award advancement. Grant only the adventure's actually earned money, possessions and narrative rewards. Any lower-level encounter-variant notes are authoring guidance for a separately revised Plan, not permission to override this declaration in play.
advancement.timing: This edition stays at level 2 throughout its authored adventure and optional continuation. It awards no XP or level increases; changing that policy requires an explicitly revised Plan.

objectives.description: Clear the winch and recover Edda before the rescue route is lost.
objectives.title: The crossing

opening_direction: Show the trapped surveyor, the approach guard and a secure place from which to assess the crossing. Explain safe fall alternatives before a risky action.
premise: A surveyor hangs below a Cairnfields crossing. Clear the approach, then keep the rescue line intact.

branches: Negotiate passage with Pell; Sena can be persuaded by his visible safety and a clear withdrawal route.
Defeat or evade the near guard, secure the rescue, and use the wall against the far guard.
Descend to the shelf and bring Edda down rather than operating the contested winch. This can bypass the second fight.
consequences: Pell’s treatment changes Sena’s response. Edda remembers whether her safety or notebook was prioritised.
A cut bridge changes the way out but does not teleport the party into another combat; allow the established lower route.
All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.
dynamic_encounter_guidance: Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.
planned_encounters: Encounter one: Pell, solo baseline AC 12, HP 7, speed 30 ft, initiative +1, club +3 for 1d4+1 bludgeoning or shortbow +3 for 1d6+1 piercing. One attack, no special powers. He surrenders when outmatched or at 2 HP. Use the referenced Rift Raider as fiction, with this weaker lookout adaptation clearly stated.

Encounter two: Sena uses the same baseline, fights from the far ledge and prioritises threatening the crossing. Her line-cutting uses a declared action and the rules for damaging that object; it never happens as a free off-turn punishment. For additional companions, add one assistant per side or use stronger admitted raiders before starting, retaining a safe retreat and exactly two prepared groups.
situations: Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Edda Sorn: an exacting surveyor with a dislocated shoulder, protective of her route notebook. She wants rescue above all and will surrender the book if that buys it. She can describe the winch and hidden lower shelf.

Pell, the near lookout: wants supplies and recognition for holding the crossing. He fears being blamed for a dead hostage. Sena, the far guard, believes rescue will be followed by an attack on their camp and cuts escape routes when threatened. Neither needs to fight to the death.

Approach encounter. A low stone wall divides the ledge. Pell can cover the winch but cannot see the lower shelf. A climb around the wall, a credible offer of provisions or a short fight can reach the mechanism. Edda calls out when she understands the plan; speaking to her is possible from safety.

The connection. Control of the near ledge allows the player to secure a spare line and operate the winch. Capture or reassure Pell and he can call across that the party only wants Edda. Drive him toward Sena and the far guard expects an assault. Their fear is evidence-based, not automatic hostility.

Extraction encounter. Sena moves along the far crossing with a blade to sever the bridge’s handline, not the separate rescue rope. Tell the player exactly which line is threatened. Two sustained efforts raise Edda to the ledge; a player can haul, protect the mechanism, negotiate or reroute the load. Dropping the notebook lightens her load but loses the survey. The lower shelf offers a bruising, recoverable fallback; establish actual falling consequences before a jump.

Ending. Edda safe on either ledge is enough to stop the encounter if the party withdraws. The raiders protect their crossing rather than pursuing forever. Edda’s employer pays 20 gp for her safe return and 5 gp more for the intact notebook; retrieving the notebook later is optional.
